Hiccups after drinking ` [Highlight start] happen when alcohol or liquid irritates your stomach, esophagus, or the nerves that control your diaphragm, causing involuntary muscle spasms and a sudden closure of your vocal cords [Highlight end] ` . Most episodes are harmless and go away on their own within a few minutes.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXLQgmUt0XgbYhSqsFB5tCyCMU6ocxxGmy61yDh1pF0vxgMpsx8C5bQDz-v4xv6LW16mmJDBUXu-nwobhHLvnD1-x69ershzD0SjXAwZTgKxelEkfsLyA3D4GFbMypVUdnQBW33wZuJlw3m7Y3u4lFMei_)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXaKZkdZItpYRdM92DTUKjgyYT6PFiS5Su351piDzi_Tcp6xVHmRYOoLlTk0-hImlDCwqxNr4oYfBe2b9RKG5eoZTVpXKH1iRNmbtEbancVrGdAMvAqBjYsk6ISQsYDg3d6ukSMPyVcl5Fy8w9_9VItHGR)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXNXRF3j21fNgxnVjYmu9SCt9OTTf72wgfYstxJ5yMUpu1KvdiDcgN-iB_aFI7ITCe6o5wg2ldtIAfXBAEJDrwTjKnnqZ9j_AnFCPCW078ZQnVzR1CT6v6II1J0BuY4BsIJhwskh_t2aUBtCVsagO0-1B5)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjgEBxCJF1891XYa3kw2vrdJkFYnov-xBrBeOR3l_BUGqvewiXYRLfjELdvONRGnUS6OZgvCzkc88zltGluNWfz6cCOxLx2iKcnjNfpS0eoAntKDr0yCNFDLqUR2gQ4GjCjMaQX9RpwRk8e4VIcCk6sJub_XuTGaRRlFbx9ubH_esbU1F21qlCthLMh8LpEWy)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXwHEIkXXUdNGEcWKCLB63DI6Ytgv546u737msJIVgDlgIF5m1COJg5691Ybs4OFGlZCkq_hiRZ7THL6tWFdqNYU1nFvj0hPJoVui5T7dSJKP1-_ZJ3cS2lspAhQZiW3p)

### Why Alcohol Triggers Hiccups

- **Stomach distension:** Drinking large amounts, beer, or carbonated mixers expands the stomach and presses upward against the diaphragm.
- **Digestive & nerve irritation:** Alcohol can irritate the stomach lining and esophagus, stimulating the vagus and phrenic nerves involved in the hiccup reflex.
- **Acid reflux:** Alcohol relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter and can increase stomach acid, irritating the esophagus.
- **Swallowing air:** Talking, laughing, or drinking/eating quickly while having drinks can cause you to swallow extra air.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXaKZkdZItpYRdM92DTUKjgyYT6PFiS5Su351piDzi_Tcp6xVHmRYOoLlTk0-hImlDCwqxNr4oYfBe2b9RKG5eoZTVpXKH1iRNmbtEbancVrGdAMvAqBjYsk6ISQsYDg3d6ukSMPyVcl5Fy8w9_9VItHGR)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXLQgmUt0XgbYhSqsFB5tCyCMU6ocxxGmy61yDh1pF0vxgMpsx8C5bQDz-v4xv6LW16mmJDBUXu-nwobhHLvnD1-x69ershzD0SjXAwZTgKxelEkfsLyA3D4GFbMypVUdnQBW33wZuJlw3m7Y3u4lFMei_)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXNXRF3j21fNgxnVjYmu9SCt9OTTf72wgfYstxJ5yMUpu1KvdiDcgN-iB_aFI7ITCe6o5wg2ldtIAfXBAEJDrwTjKnnqZ9j_AnFCPCW078ZQnVzR1CT6v6II1J0BuY4BsIJhwskh_t2aUBtCVsagO0-1B5)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXX98Ch6GrM2xvUhehRFMVblvNY9tKWbrEf0P-dwbc_R4d8lM2c_m66KxFfG8Otx9uPi_I3ABqDBNW1Jq4xxjWPI_wMnUeOrz9z5z7WqFjdzf2G7IKLaAOvzDdhuSAOUZucgHbXbT7zetBIcFSHkw_K)

On a [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESpgEBxCJF14O6slovNDGiTMMUDq9kkKw6v8hJBw6xhg_It8gcXxX1iSQ_s_0jRuYpjDR9D_O6rdesO2-Nzl39_JKVhZ4FpZ8Sux0lXxAOsedw7WqL0VXNUytYGWX4rTXbvJBGN--IXAbhuvI1Dk1b77W72wQy_if2VFFhzKk214cRsHEI6xBfg5kb-Qd9YSukttCep6mXuwiu9nrz9trHYMz0yWbDAGRI) thread about frequent alcohol-induced hiccups, opinions on the topic differ—some note that carbonation and a full stomach trigger the spasms, while others report getting them even with non-carbonated drinks.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESpgEBxCJF14O6slovNDGiTMMUDq9kkKw6v8hJBw6xhg_It8gcXxX1iSQ_s_0jRuYpjDR9D_O6rdesO2-Nzl39_JKVhZ4FpZ8Sux0lXxAOsedw7WqL0VXNUytYGWX4rTXbvJBGN--IXAbhuvI1Dk1b77W72wQy_if2VFFhzKk214cRsHEI6xBfg5kb-Qd9YSukttCep6mXuwiu9nrz9trHYMz0yWbDAGRI)

### Ways to Stop Them
Evidence for home remedies is mostly anecdotal, though they often aim to reset breathing or stimulate the vagus nerve:[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXNXRF3j21fNgxnVjYmu9SCt9OTTf72wgfYstxJ5yMUpu1KvdiDcgN-iB_aFI7ITCe6o5wg2ldtIAfXBAEJDrwTjKnnqZ9j_AnFCPCW078ZQnVzR1CT6v6II1J0BuY4BsIJhwskh_t2aUBtCVsagO0-1B5)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXwHEIkXXUdNGEcWKCLB63DI6Ytgv546u737msJIVgDlgIF5m1COJg5691Ybs4OFGlZCkq_hiRZ7THL6tWFdqNYU1nFvj0hPJoVui5T7dSJKP1-_ZJ3cS2lspAhQZiW3p)

- Sip cold water slowly.
- Hold your breath briefly or try the Valsalva maneuver (exhaling gently against a closed mouth and pinched nose).
- Swallow a spoonful of sugar or try a small bite of something sour/tart like a lemon.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXwYicYfkWmdximaT3jdRYvR-OKok9eCRLK-hyFmHaybcdJd9Eg3Y0zVpgNC3-PVy2-HExOAuDIoaY5E1671j4NdDptaIeoH9WrbnDp-JKBC4UulC4vJ2ScuhYOb-3y_71hpkKkFL3h5-Fx8X3xl9ub0gIGvRWtzVn)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXaKZkdZItpYRdM92DTUKjgyYT6PFiS5Su351piDzi_Tcp6xVHmRYOoLlTk0-hImlDCwqxNr4oYfBe2b9RKG5eoZTVpXKH1iRNmbtEbancVrGdAMvAqBjYsk6ISQsYDg3d6ukSMPyVcl5Fy8w9_9VItHGR)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXLQgmUt0XgbYhSqsFB5tCyCMU6ocxxGmy61yDh1pF0vxgMpsx8C5bQDz-v4xv6LW16mmJDBUXu-nwobhHLvnD1-x69ershzD0SjXAwZTgKxelEkfsLyA3D4GFbMypVUdnQBW33wZuJlw3m7Y3u4lFMei_)

### Prevention & When to See a Doctor
To lower your chances next time, drink slowly, moderate intake, eat beforehand, and cut back on carbonated or acidic mixers.
